records.utterance: *Stands up, eyes red, looking at you and the others. His lips move, but nothing comes out.*
records.response_truth: Get on it. Answer it. Tell them our position, tell them we're four survivors, tell them we have injured - go, now, talk.
records.response_pred: Hey, it's alright. Let's sit down for a minute. You don't have to say anything, just breathe. We all know what we're going through, it's okay to feel like this. We'll get through this together.

records.utterance: These past few days… I know I haven't been easy to be around.
records.response_truth:
No, you haven't. But you kept us alive. The rationing plan, the water scout, the raft timeline, the log - that was all you. The crackers thing happened and we dealt with it and it's done.

You're not easy to be around but I'd rather have you here than not. So don't apologize for being who you are. Just keep doing what you do.

Now make sure DaVinci is giving them the right coordinates and not just shouting "we're alive" into a radio.
records.response_pred:
No, no you haven't been easy but I understand why. I'm not saying it's been a breeze, this is a stressful situation. But it's not like we can't handle it, we've been handling it, that's what we do. So let's not dwell on it, let's focus on what we've got - water, shelter, supplies, and the signal. That's all we need to worry about right now. We stick to the plan and we get out of here.

Before we move on though - what's the plan for tonight? Fire, shelter, food, water? I need to know so I can organize the jobs. I can't have people doing the same thing at the same time, that's just a waste of energy. And if you've got something specific in mind, let me know. I'm not going to argue with you about it - I just need a clear plan so I can organize the team.

So what's the plan?

records.utterance: *The three of them drift apart, each doing their own thing. No one takes charge. The silence settles over the camp.*
records.response_truth:
Three hours. Nobody needs to be doing anything urgent right now.

Leave the camp. Seriously. Leave it. We built it to survive in, not to live in, and rescue teams deal with crash sites all the time. Pack your personal stuff, anything you actually want to keep, but don't spend the next three hours tidying wreckage like you're checking out of a hotel.

Michelangelo, good. Stay there. Watch the sky. You've earned it.

DaVinci, slow down, you've got three hours, you're not going to miss the helicopter because you didn't pack fast enough.

Donatello - whatever's in that notebook, keep it. Genuinely. That log is probably going to matter for the accident investigation and you should hand it over when they ask.

I'm going to go sit by the SOS for a bit. Just to be there when they come in. Feels right.
records.response_pred:
Alright, let's take a second here. We've all got our heads screwed on backwards right now, so let's get a handle on what we've actually got. First things first - what exactly are we working with? Donatello, take a look at the supplies, see if we've got any food, water, or any medical stuff. And while you're doing that, let's figure out where we are. Any idea what the terrain looks like around here? We need to know if we're close to a river or a stream, or anything like that. That's priority number one - finding water.

DaVinci, you're good with fire, right? Then get a fire going, or gather the materials we'll need to do that. We'll need it to signal for help if we can't find water.

Michelangelo, I need you to go through every bag, every pocket, every compartment that's still intact. Look specifically for water bottles, anything sealed, anything liquid. Also any lighters, matches, foil blankets, rope or cord, anything sharp. Don't touch anything that looks like it could be a hazard, just call it out.

Donatello, since you're apparently in an agreeable mood, let's talk about something. The empty drink bottle I found in the wreckage the other day, the one that wasn't part of the rationing plan - I need to know what's going on with that. And while we're at it, what happened to the firewood? That pile is basically nothing. We need that tonight, same as we needed it last night. I'm not having a go, I just need to know if you're okay because you've been sitting there for a while and it's not like you to just... stop.

What's going on with you?

records.utterance: I dreamed about home last night.
records.response_truth: Yeah? Good dream or just... home?
records.response_pred: Alright, but we've got work to do. What did you see? Any details I should know about? We need to focus on what we've got here and the tasks at hand. Priorities, mate. We can dwell on the past later. What's the state of the camp? Any issues we need to address?

Look, I understand the impulse but that's not how this works. Emergencies are what we're in right now, and if that's what this is for, then it's already been used.

We need to share this food equally, not hoard it. If you're hungry, eat. If the rationing plan says 200ml, that's what it says. We can't just take more because we think we might need it later. That's how people starve.

And for the record, if you're taking supplies for yourself while you're also the one who wrote the rationing plan, that's a problem. We're all in this together, and we need to trust each other to do what's right for the group.

So either you give that water back or we talk about this like adults and decide how to divide it fairly. But whatever happens, we can't have you taking more than your share.

Let's focus on what we can control right now - finding water, making shelter, and keeping the signal going. We'll figure out the rest when we get there. But we can't do any of that if we're not all working together. So let's put aside any personal concerns and focus on the task at hand.

Now, let's get to work. We need to find more water and make sure we're as sheltered as we can be before nightfall. Let's go.

records.utterance: I logged every resource and decision from these five days. I'm going to write it up as a proper report when we get back. On the last page I left myself a question I haven't answered yet — if you had to do it over, what would you change?
records.response_truth:
Honestly? I'd have pushed harder on group transparency from day one. The crackers, the drink, DaVinci and the reef plan, Michelangelo sitting on the flight path information - all of it came out eventually but it came out sideways, in bits, usually because someone noticed something and came to me privately. That's not a system, that's just luck.

If I'd set the expectation on day one that everything gets said out loud to everyone, not to me, not in whispers, but actually to the group - I think we'd have wasted less energy on things that weren't really problems once they were in the open.

The other thing is Michelangelo. I kept telling him to push through, to get up, to do the task. And he did, mostly, but I was treating his mental state as an obstacle to manage rather than a resource to actually work with. He noticed everything. He was the early warning system for half the problems in this camp. I should have figured that out on day one instead of day three.

What's your answer? You wrote the question, you've had the whole stay to think about it. What would you change?
records.response_pred:
Look, I'm not going to sugarcoat it - this was a mess. We made some bad calls, we missed some things, we didn't communicate well enough, and we let some tensions simmer that shouldn't have.

If I had to do it over, here's what I'd change:

1. Better resource management: We should have been more vigilant about rationing our supplies from the start, and we should have had a clear, fair system in place from the get-go.

2. Clearer leadership: I should have made decisions more decisively and communicated them clearly to the group. I let things slide because I didn't want to rock the boat, but that just led to confusion and resentment.

3. Better teamwork: I should have listened more to everyone's ideas and opinions, and I should have encouraged open communication instead of letting things fester.

4. Prioritizing mental health: I should have recognized earlier that everyone was struggling mentally, and I should have made more of an effort to address it. We all need to take care of ourselves as well as each other.

5. Being prepared for the worst: I should have had a contingency plan in case rescue didn't come. We were all hoping for the best, but we should have been ready for the worst.

So, those are the changes I'd make if I had to do it over. But the important thing is that we learned from this experience, and we can use it to improve how we work together in the future. That's the only way we're going to survive out here.

records.utterance: First thing when I get back — I'm going to compile all the resource data from these five days into a report.
records.response_truth:
Yeah, do it. That data is actually useful beyond just the investigation - if it gets into the right hands it could genuinely inform how people prepare for and respond to this kind of situation. Don't let it sit in a drawer somewhere.

Send me a copy when it's done. I mean that.
records.response_pred: Sounds good to me. Just make sure it's thorough and includes everything we've used, found, and estimated to have left. Don't forget to note any changes in condition or usefulness of items. And when you're done, we'll all go through it together to make sure it's accurate and complete.

None. They served no practical purpose at all.

That's the point.

DaVinci finds comfort in that sort of thing, it's his way of working through things. And if they help keep his spirits up, that makes the rest of us feel better too. So while they didn't directly help us survive, they did help us keep going.

Donatello, you and I can scout north toward that treeline, look for any sign of a stream or runoff, low ground, animal trails, anything like that. We take one water bottle, leave one here. Two hours out, turn back if we find nothing.

DaVinci stays here, keeps working on fire and shelter, and Michelangelo finishes the full inventory sweep. When we get back we reassess.

Donatello, check the first-aid kit, make sure we've got everything we need for the trip. DaVinci, secure the fire, we might need it later.
